key_insight: Variance-guided measurement group construction (VGMC) reduces molecular energy estimation variance by redesigning which Pauli terms share measurement shots, not just optimizing existing measurement bases.
engineering_relevance: VGMC offers a route to lower sampling costs in variational quantum simulation while retaining local measurements compatible with current and near-term devices.
method: Include every Hamiltonian term measurable in each existing basis, then jointly optimize estimator coefficients and shot allocations.
Score candidate groups by expected benefit versus the cost of withdrawing shots from existing bases.
Greedily construct qubit-wise commuting groups and jointly re-optimize the expanded measurement design.
evidence_signal: With exact covariances, VGMC reduced variance by 18.19%–23.38% versus state-of-the-art methods on molecular benchmarks where it added bases; gains persisted with approximate covariances, and finite-shot simulations indicated lower shot requirements near chemical accuracy.
watch_item: Practical savings depend on covariance quality and must be weighed against the overhead of estimating covariances and constructing additional measurement bases.
paper_title: From optimization to construction: Expanding quantum measurement designs
